facts.statement: The IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2025 were published on 19 February 2025, repealing the FM Regulations 2022, and create three FME categories: Retail, Non-Retail and Authorised.
FME net-worth tiers under the 2025 regime: Authorised FME USD 75,000; Registered FME (Non-Retail) USD 500,000; Registered FME (Retail) USD 1,000,000.
facts.detail: Retail FME track record: 5 years managing USD 200 million+ AUM with 25,000+ investors, or a key shareholder with 25%+ holding having USD 50 million AUM, 1,000+ investors and USD 2 million net worth.

facts.statement: Scheme thresholds under FM Regs 2025: Venture Capital Scheme min corpus USD 3 million / max USD 200 million / max 50 investors; Angel Scheme min USD 1 million / max 200 investors per segregated portfolio; Restricted Scheme min USD 3 million / max 1,000 investors; Retail Scheme min USD 3 million / min 20 investors / no maximum.
facts.detail: Open-ended Restricted/Retail schemes may start at USD 1 million and must reach USD 3 million within 12 months.

facts.statement: Investment minimum tickets: VC scheme USD 250,000 (non-accredited) or USD 60,000 for FME employees; Angel USD 40,000 (non-accredited); Restricted USD 150,000 (non-accredited) or USD 40,000 for employees/directors; Retail has no minimum except close-ended schemes investing 15-50% in unlisted securities (USD 10,000). Accredited investors are exempt from minimums.

Skin-in-the-game requirements: VC schemes 2.5-10%; Restricted schemes open-ended 5-10% and closed-ended 2.5-10%; Retail schemes 1% or USD 200,000 whichever is lower. A custodian is mandatory above USD 70 million scheme size.

The 8 April 2025 transition circular increased PPM validity from 6 to 12 months, reduced the minimum corpus from USD 5 million to USD 3 million, and offered a one-time PPM extension: re-file within 3 months at 50% of the fresh scheme filing fee for an additional 6 months' validity; the processing fee is waived when the re-filing is necessitated by Authority action.

FM amendments approved 22 December 2025: KMP eligibility relaxed via certification; PPM validity may be extended multiple times for VC/Restricted schemes; a one-time 3-month extension for expired PPMs; and a 24-month custodian migration window (notified 2 February 2026).
The Third-Party Fund Management ('platform play') framework with fee structure was issued 24 July 2025 and 8 September 2025, capping third-party managed corpus at USD 50 million per scheme.
The IFSCA Stewardship Code - a voluntary framework for responsible investment and ESG integration - went to consultation in August 2025 and was issued by circular in October 2025.

Fund management growth: 114 FMEs (FY24) to 162 FMEs and 229 schemes (FY25, +42%), commitments USD 15.74 billion (FY25); September 2025 snapshot: 310 FME registrations, 194 schemes, commitments USD 26.30 billion, funds raised USD 12.27 billion, investments USD 13.22 billion, 4,733 investors (57% NRI/OCI, 37% resident), 23 relocated schemes with USD 9.14 billion commitments.
facts.detail: FY25 composition: 78 Cat I/II AIFs with USD 4,517 million AUM; 135 Cat III AIFs with USD 3,516 million AUM; PMS 23 FMEs managing USD 1.18 billion.
facts.source_ref: fund management chapter; FM ecosystem report; brochure

facts.statement: Tax-neutral relocation of offshore funds to GIFT IFSC is available until 31 March 2030, and the first 10 ESG schemes received a fee waiver.

Under the earlier FM Regulations 2022 (effective 19 May 2022) an Authorised FME had minimum investor ticket USD 250,000 with max 50 investors and VC corpus USD 5-200 million with minimum tenor 3 years; Registered Non-Retail required PPM filing 21 working days prior; Registered Retail required minimum 4 directors and 3 KMPs; ESG disclosure was mandatory for FMEs above USD 3 billion AUM; PMS minimum ticket was USD 150,000; Family Investment Fund needed USD 10 million within 3 years; Special Situation Funds were close-ended with minimum tenor 3 years.
facts.detail: Largely superseded by the 2025 Regulations - useful for old-vs-new trap questions.
